extracted.intended_audience: museum staff completing IMLS Museums for America (MFA) applications and IMLS/evaluator staff conducting the MFA evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: This page is an appendix from the IMLS MFA program evaluation containing descriptive statistics for requests/awards and the full survey/interview/site-visit protocols used to collect information from museums about MFA applications, unfunded applications, and awarded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive statistics reported for applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications and awards the report presents: Count, Total Request/Total Award Amount, Total % (of funding), Mean request/award amount, Median request/award amount, Minimum total request/award, Maximum total request/award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statistics are reported by grouping (museum discipline, museum size, region, and state) to describe distribution of requests and awards (see Exhibits B-1 through B-8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum groupings for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Application and award statistics are disaggregated by museum discipline group, museum size (small/medium/large), region, and state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these groupings when comparing funding patterns and when calculating the descriptive statistics listed above.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1:1 cost sharing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMLS Museums for America grant program requires museums to commit to a 1:1 cost sharing for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey asks whether cost sharing caused museums not to apply and whether it impacted time to raise funds, type of grant applied for, project duration, scope, staffing costs, and non-labor costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections respondents must complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents will be asked to complete only those survey sections applicable to their MFA background: A. Museum Background; B. Most Recent Application Process; C. Most Recent Unfunded Application; D. Awarded Project Partners and Activities; E. Awarded Project Short Term Effects; F. Awarded Project Long Term Effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey includes each museum’s recent application and/or awarded project data for reference. Multiple people may complete different sections; the last person to complete submits the final version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application identification fields required
rubrics_metrics.description: For the most recent application respondents are asked to supply: Project Title, Fiscal Year, Funded (yes/no), Contact First Name/Last Name, Contact Title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent is not the most knowledgeable person, they are instructed to pass the survey to the appropriate person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-sharing impact items
rubrics_metrics.description: If cost-sharing had an impact on the proposed project, respondents indicate effect on: (a) Amount of time to raise cost sharing funds; (b) Type of MFA grant applied for; (c) Duration of the proposed project; (d) Scope of the proposed project; (e) Staffing costs of the proposed project; (f) Non-labor costs of the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents select No / Yes / Don't know for each row.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who wrote the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents indicate which description(s) apply to the person(s) who wrote the MFA application: (a) Dedicated staffed grant writer; (b) Hired grant writer(s) as consultant; (c) Administrative leadership; (d) Other staff member(s); (e) Other; (f) Don't know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple responses allowed to capture authorship/roles in application development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior reviewer/panelist experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents indicate whether anyone on their staff has served as: (a) Field reviewer for the MFA grant program; (b) Grant review panelist for the MFA grant program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer options: Yes / No / Don't know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and participation in outreach activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents report awareness of, participation in, and helpfulness of IMLS outreach activities: (a) Information sessions at conferences; (b) Information from associations regarding MFA application; (c) Audio conference calls prior to deadlines; (d) Individual counseling via phone/email/in-person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response scale: Was not aware / Was aware but did not participate / Participated and activity was not at all helpful / Participated and somewhat helpful / Participated and very helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and use of IMLS web resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents report awareness, utilization, and helpfulness of resources on the IMLS website such as: (a) Sample MFA applications and tips; (b) Outcome-based evaluation resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same five-point utilization/helpfulness scale as outreach activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS does not track reapplications
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that IMLS DOES NOT track reapplications; therefore each application, whether a reapplication or not, is treated individually and on its own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey asks whether respondents were aware of this policy (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process effects on institution
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent the application process prompted museums to: (a) Create a mission/strategic plan for the first time; (b) Revise existing mission/strategic plan; (c) Increase awareness of different programming; (d) Increase awareness of resources/strengths; (e) Reframe project to fit IMLS categories; (f) Adopt new ways of integrating outcomes-based planning; (g) Explore new external partnerships; (h) Collaborate among departments/staff; (i) Explore new technologies; (j) Improve ability to apply for other funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond using Not at all affected / Somewhat affected / Affected a lot / Don't know, and can specify up to two other application effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinions on application process clarity and ease
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents rate agreement with statements about the application process: (a) Information about MFA opportunities was easy to obtain; (b) MFA guidelines and requirements were clear; (c) Instructions on budget (direct, indirect costs, cost-sharing) were clear; (d) Evaluation requirements were clear; (e) MFA grant-review process was clear; (f) Downloading application from Grants.gov was easy; (g) Submitting online through Grants.gov was easy; (h) IMLS staff was helpful regarding Grants.gov; (i) Submitting by hand/mail was easier than using Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response scale: Strongly disagree / Disagree / Agree / Strongly agree / Don't know or not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative difficulty of MFA application
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents indicate whether the MFA application process is more difficult, the same, or less difficult than: (a) Other Federal grants; (b) Other government grants (state/local); (c) Private grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select More difficult / Same / Less difficult / Don't know for each comparator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of applying again and reasons for non-application
rubrics_metrics.description: How likely the museum will apply for another MFA grant (Not at all likely / Somewhat likely / Very likely / Don't know) and, if not likely, indicate reasons (check all that apply) such as: already have an application; mission/strategic plan not current; unavailable resources to plan/write application; unavailable/inefficient resources to carry out project if awarded; difficulty finding cost-sharing funds; funding not needed; discouraged by previous failed applications; application requires unavailable hardware/software; plus two open 'other' reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-text field available for additional reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open recommendations for improving application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents may enter recommendations for improving the MFA application process or 'None.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-text input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded application background and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: For most recent unfunded application respondents are asked whether it was a redesign/resubmission of a previous unfunded project, whether they resubmitted it to a different IMLS grant program, whether they received IMLS funding from a non-MFA program for the application, whether they submitted it to a non-IMLS funder, and whether they received funding from that non-IMLS funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer options: Yes / No / Don't know for each item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution and opinions on unfunded application
rubrics_metrics.description: For unfunded applications respondents report whether they were able to execute any version of the unfunded project (Yes/No/Don't know) and rate agreement with statements: (a) We believe our application was given full and fair consideration; (b) Reviewer's comments were useful for redesigning the project; (c) IMLS staff was helpful in providing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response scale: Strongly disagree / Disagree / Agree / Strongly agree / Don't know/Not applicable. Open-text prompt: 'What other aspects of the unfunded application should IMLS know about?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded project identification and knowledge level
rubrics_metrics.description: For awarded projects respondents supply Project Title, Award From/To dates, Number of Extensions, contact info, and indicate their level of knowledge about the awarded project (Very knowledgeable / Somewhat knowledgeable / No one affiliated is knowledgeable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent is not the most knowledgeable person, they are instructed to have that person complete the survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award project type classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents indicate the type of awarded project: ongoing continuation of a prior awarded project; new project likely/did lead to a continuation application (not an extension); new project which will not/did not lead to a continuation application (not an extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification captures project continuity and intent to continue beyond the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey administration procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey administration instructions include: use navigation buttons (do not use browser Back/Forward), Save Progress and Exit to allow multiple people to complete sections, the last person to complete submits the final version, complete by a specified deadline (e.g., November 24, 2010), and contact technical support for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical contact provided (John Parsons at RMC Research) with email and phone. Passwords expire after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey login authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents must enter Museum User Name and password supplied to their organization to access the survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Login screen includes 'Reset Form' and 'Proceed to Survey' controls; technical contact listed for password retrieval.
